gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The two countries signed a peace ___ (TREAT).
gaps.explanation: A peace treaty is a formal agreement; 'treatment' means medical care or the way you behave towards someone.

gaps.sentence: The island is ___ , with no permanent residents (HABIT).
gaps.explanation: 'No permanent residents' shows the negative: uninhabited (un- + inhabited). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (PROSPER) of the region depends on tourism.
The campaign aims to raise ___ of road safety (AWARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ness forms the noun: raise awareness is the fixed phrase; 'aware' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: He felt he was ___ for the work he did, so he asked for a raise (PAY).
gaps.hint: paid too little — he wants a raise (under-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix under- means too little: underpaid means paid less than deserved, which explains asking for a raise.
